question: Why do poorer households in Britain often pay more than others for the very same energy, insurance and credit?
answer: Because the cheapest deals go to those who can pay by direct debit, borrow from a bank and shop online. Prepayment meters, cash payments, high-cost loans and postcode-priced insurance add up: researchers at Bristol put the average poverty premium at about £490 a year. Being short of money is itself expensive.
move: Ask what a price assumes about the buyer before calling it the price.
ask: Which bill would cost me less if I changed how I pay it rather than what I buy?
source: Davies, Finney and Hartfree, University of Bristol, 2016
reference: Davies, Finney & Hartfree, Paying to Be Poor: Uncovering the Scale and Nature of the Poverty Premium, University of Bristol Personal Finance Research Centre, 2016
